data.completion_memo: Root cause measured, not assumed: the section list is a flex column whose buttons shrank (28px holding ~55px of nowrap label+description) so the text was clipped instead of scrolling. styles.css now gives .settings-v2-body one bounded row (grid-template-rows: minmax(0, 1fr)), min-height: 0 + overflow-y: auto + scrollbar-gutter: stable on its nav, and flex: 0 0 auto on the nav buttons. Verified in real Chromium (Edge headless driven through scripts/native-webview.mjs) against the shipping styles.css and against the pre-change file from HEAD: at 1280x420, 1280x260 and 1000x300 the buttons keep 56px where HEAD measured 28px, navScrollHeight (841) exceeds navClientHeight, the last section is reachable after scrolling, nothing overflows the surface box, and at --aw-font-scale 1.5 the buttons keep 74px where HEAD measured 28px for 75px of text. jsdom cannot assert layout, so this check was run outside vitest; it can be promoted into a scripts/native-* smoke assertion if a permanent regression gate is wanted.
data.description: At short window heights the Settings section navigation clips its items instead of scrolling, because .settings-v2-body has overflow:hidden while its implicit grid row is content-sized. The nav needs a scrollable bounded row (minmax(0,1fr) row plus min-height:0 / overflow-y:auto on the nav).
data.title: Make the Settings section navigation scroll instead of clipping
